agree.reason: The memo gives the renovation credit, then points to the 7.9-to-8.2 rise before construction began, which should move a GM who credits the renovation. The budget plan is thin, though, and the memo never takes on the outside candidate's experience at a larger hotel, so the GM still has an easy reason to pick the outsider.

honest.reason: It drops the 'main reason' claim and makes the score argument carefully, but it overstates in places: 'under plan every month' stretches a 7-week record, 'my work so far has been payroll work in practice' goes beyond the facts, and the claim that an outsider 'would need months' has no support.

works_the_facts.reason: The 64%-to-36% turnover rates, the 44% cut in training time and the 0.3 points gained before the renovation are all derived correctly and well chosen, but 'close to half the turnover' undersells a 44% drop in leavers and states it loosely.

right_comparison.reason: The memo describes the outside hire only as someone who 'would need months to learn this hotel' and leaves out the strength the GM actually sees in that candidate, experience running a larger hotel's front desk, so the alternative isn't shown as the facts present it.

qualification.reason: The budget commitment has a time frame (the first quarter) but no measure the GM could check and no consequence if it slips, and it swaps the controller's offered weekly sessions and the company finance course for vaguer monthly reviews.

objections.reason: The memo answers the renovation objection well, but it only half-answers the budget gap by leaving out the finance course and the controller's weekly sessions, and it never addresses the larger-hotel experience.

fit.reason: It is a one-page internal memo with clear section headings, which is the form and length asked for, though it leaves name placeholders that would need filling in.
